abandon: m04 says the RL-written examples work by giving the base a prior over answer length (and closing habit), so that it writes longer answers and stops giving quick finished-wrong ones. It explains draw 2's null by saying draw 2's examples were shorter or less checked. The board already rules out that account. (1) Draw 2 moved the base's output length as much as draw 1 did, yet gained nothing. result-6d422d gives draw 1 as '435/497 tokens 4400 | cue + 3 examples written by Math-RL in context'. result-5227b9 gives draw 2 as 'score: base MATH-500 401/494 tokens 4361 | cue + 3 examples written by Math-RL in context (draw 2)', against 'Math-RL-written draw 1 432 (+5.7 [2.6, 8.7]), draw 2 401 (-0.6 [-4.5, 3.2])'. Tokens per problem were 4,400 vs 4,361, a ratio of 1.01, so the length prior moved equally in both draws. The 28-problem difference therefore cannot come from 'the two sets differ in length'. The same holds for the base-written sets: draw 2 produced longer answers than draw 1 and did no better (result-6d422d '414/497 tokens 3380'; result-5227b9 '403/494 tokens 3741'). (2) Without length, the only channel left is the closing re-check, and the board rules that out too. result-855858: 'RL does not win by checking more' and 'markers do not separate right from wrong samples of the same model and problem'. result-882fa7: raising the base's Wait/check rate to RL's level gives '+0.5 pts [-2.2, +3.1]', and 'the push adds the word without a check'. (3) On hard328 the longer prior from the same draw-1 examples gave 'RL-written draw 1 164/328 vs 164 (0.0 [-4.3, 4.3]; 26 problems only with, 26 only without), cap hits 107 vs 77' (result-5227b9), so where answers did get longer there was no net gain. The mechanism's first test (median n_new of draw 1 over draw 2 >= 1.2, refuted below 1.05) is already implied to fail by the board's own mean-token figures (ratio 1.01). The draw-1 vs draw-2 difference has to come from something in the example texts other than their length, such as a copied answer: result-6d422d notes '2 RL-arm answers copy an example's answer'.
